summary.one_liner: Alacritty is a fast, cross-platform, OpenGL-based terminal emulator that aims for sensible defaults with extensive configuration.
summary.what_it_does: Alacritty is a terminal emulator that runs on BSD, Linux, macOS and Windows. It is built around OpenGL rendering and integrates with other applications rather than reimplementing their functionality. Configuration is done through a TOML file (alacritty.toml), which it looks for in several XDG, home-directory and /etc locations, or %APPDATA% on Windows; the file is not created automatically. Documentation is available as the man page `man 5 alacritty` or on the project website. The README states the project is at beta readiness, with some missing features and bugs, and that it is used as a daily driver by many. Precompiled binaries for macOS and Windows are on the GitHub releases page. The project deliberately omits tabs, splits and a GUI config editor, recommending a window manager or terminal multiplexer such as tmux for those.
use_cases: daily-driver terminal on macOS, Linux, Windows or BSD
configuring a terminal via a TOML file
running tmux or a window manager alongside a fast terminal
how_to_run: Install via a package manager on Linux, BSD, macOS or Windows (see the installation instructions)
Or download a prebuilt binary for macOS or Windows from the GitHub releases page
notable: Cross-platform: BSD, Linux, macOS and Windows
Configured via alacritty.toml with multiple standard config locations
Deliberately omits tabs and splits, leaving them to window managers or multiplexers
caveats: README describes the software as beta, with some missing features and bugs
Requires at least OpenGL ES 2.0; Windows needs ConPTY (Windows 10 version 1809 or higher)
No tabs, splits, or GUI config editor by design
